If they cared about minimalism, they wouldn’t have ugly gradients from 2006, poor item spacing across the entire app, poorly chosen and inconsistent icons, and ugly backgrounds with no option of customizing them. If they knew anything about real design, they wouldn’t say “design is subjective”. It looks like it was designed by a second semester design intern. 

I don’t have the energy to do a full design crit of the app in an app store review. But this silly developer response was enough for me to stop using the app. They clearly are just coasting at this point and have no desire to make the app better anymore.

reviews.text: Ugh! I thought my search was over…. Just downloaded the app ~30min ago. It’s already heading to the bin. A star given for the overall first impression of the interface. In many ways it borrows or models itself after Apple’s own native apps, which IMHO is terrific. However, 3 stars off bc Anydo ultimately failed to meet a couple minimal expectations: 1) INCONSISTENT FONT SIZE. I have good vision but the font type and size in the app are inconsistent. Some places have mouse-font that can barely be seen. (I expect this for certain calendar views but not anywhere else.) Can’t find app specific controls to adjust this. 2) CAN’T FIND CONTROLS TO DELETE INDIVIDUAL LIST ITEMS. I know they’re in there somewhere but even using Anydo FAQ, can’t find it. For example, building a grocery list adding items works much like Apple’s Reminder app which, again, terrific. However deleting individual items from that list is challenging. I can only find controls to delete the entire grocery list. Swiping, press/hold nor any menu I could find has worked. I now realize the same is true on other lists. Perhaps my growing frustration blinded me from seeing the obvious but that is EXACTLY why I’m considering deleting the app. I don’t want an app that drains my time and energy figuring out how to do easy things. I want to get in/out of the app quickly. I don’t want list making to become another time draining task that gets in the way of actually doing. If deleting a grocery list item turned into a 30min speed bump, what happens if I try to use Anydo for something important? Shame. The initial impression showed such promise…That all said, Anydo has stood the test of time and has many devoted followers. That’s a HUGE accomplishment. For that, I give a second star out of respect.

reviews.text:
Close, but not quite. Such good potential wasted by essentially being converted into a clunky sales pitch. 

Visually, the app appealing, easy to navigate, and makes sense contextually. There are all the “must-have” features like calendar integrations, lists and labels, reminders and deadlines and such, but the efficacy is lost with notifications, banners, badges, and an entire section of the main page dedicated to showing you all the value of the paid subscription aspects still available to you if you’d only pay the monthly price of yada yada…

Another significant hindrance is the difficulty in trying to join in to another user’s board, unless that’s simply another feature available for purchase. I could see this working for someone who was going to be the sole user of the lists, but unless you’re willing to pay, it’s not quite a team application. 

On a personal level, I found that seeing so many “call to action” pitches throughout the app was not only distracting, but quickly got annoying. One or two. That’s all we need. I know where the buttons are, I clicked on them before, I’ll remember if I do decide to upgrade where I need to go. In a time of software as a service and subscription models galore, this felt a little too heavy-handed and stood out for the sales pitch it is. 

Three out of five, works fine enough I guess, but download it and try it out, I’m not your boss, I can’t tell you what to do with your life, be a free spirit, fly on the breezes of the App Store as far as your little wings will take you.

 UPDATE 2: responding to the developers’ response to me: I didn’t know that Apple forced some things on developers however, condescension in response to something that most users would not know is not appreciated and the smiley emoji doesn’t help. The issue with this app continuing to scroll through upcoming alerts without telling you the date it is due (it only lists the time) has caused me to miss repeating tasks because I mark them done when the alert isn’t due until a later date. Another issue is that in order to save your date and time, you have to click DONE in the lower right corner but if you are clicking to indicate that the task is completed, you do so with DONE in the lower right corner. They either need to change it to DONE and COMPLETE, or SAVE and DONE. I’ve often inadvertently marked a task as complete when I only intended to save a change. Users should know that this app is much easier to use on Android than on iOS and that there are features that can cause them to miss appointments. 
 
UPDATE: I was finally able to get the app to load on my new iPhone X. I have used it on an Android for years. There are a couple of features I didn’t care for on Android (it stops you from doing anything when the alerts pop up and sometimes made me lose what I was writing) but I prefer that to the iPhone version. There is no easy way to snooze the alert like there is on Android so you have to click to go into the app to do it. But when you do, it scrolls through all of the alerts you have set without telling you when they are. So I end up marking repeating tasks or something I have previously snoozed as done because I can’t see that that alert is for a later time. When trying to set an alert, I generally write something like, “Dr appt at 3:00” and set my alert for 2 so I’m not late. Sometimes, I set an alert for the night before so I am prepared for the change in my schedule. But if you do that, The app WILL NOT LET YOU CHANGE THE DAY OR TIME! It auto fills the date as today and the time as 3 and you can’t change it. In order to get around this, you have to enter the time and date in the app first, then what it’s for. However, it will sometimes still default to the time it wants you to set rather than the one you set. If my appointment is at 3, I don’t want an alert at 3. I’m already there! 🙄 And I would like to just write the date and time in rather than having to scroll through the flip menu. Additionally, if you don’t remember to set am/pm FIRST, the app won’t let you set the time correctly. So if it’s 2:00 am and I want to set my alert for 1:00 pm, The app absolutely will not let me and keeps changing the time until I fix the am/pm issue. It can be helpful to have it do that if I was trying to save the alert for a time in the past, but not being able to fill it in in order (day/time/am or pm) is frustrating. If you have to fill in am/pm first, then put that before the time. In my initial review, I said I would give it a 4.5 if I could get it to load but on second thought, I would give it a 4 in the Android version due to the issues I mentioned and a 3 in the iPhone version. The help desk did help me figure out how to get it to load, though it took a day after they said they solved the problem (too many completed but not deleted tasks) before it actually loaded and didn’t crash, and I appreciate that! I feel like this app is so close but it continues to be frustrating to use. I can’t find anything better so I’ll probably stick with it, though.

reviews.text:
Cancelled subscription due to sharing issues and annoying features. When I started paying for this app, it was fairly simple and worked well to share shopping and todo lists with my wife. Over the years, the features have multiplied, bugs have multiplied, and I feel like I’m being strong-armed into using features that aren’t helpful and are actively annoying. Sharing and syncing issues were the straw that broke me.

First, the unwanted features. Any.do created lists I did not want, and I was unable to delete them after hours of trying and googling. Any.do started using artificial stupidity to automatically add due dates to items: “2-3 avocados” turned into an “avocados” item due on February 3rd. Any.do decided it needed to organize my grocery list, but of course it doesn’t know where anything is in my grocery store, and it makes all kinds of bad guesses about what things are.

That’s only a taste of the “advanced” features that were forced on me in a barely working state. Have you ever had somebody insist on helping you, and they’re so incompetent that you prefer to be left alone, but they won’t take a hint? That’s Any.do. For each new feature, there was a learning curve to figure out how to avoid accidentally activating it. That was no accident, Any.do was desperate for me to start using these features that didn’t serve any purpose for me.

But I might have continued to tolerate it if we hadn’t had chronic issues with sharing. I don’t think I have ever been able to delete a list that I shared with my wife. She couldn’t leave the list, I couldn’t remove her from it, and neither of us could delete it. The final straw was my wife being unable to sync our grocery list and me not being able to fix it after twenty minutes of trying, including uninstalling and reinstalling the app. That’s the end for me, and I feel relieved.

Two stars instead of one because we got a few years of utility out of it despite the issues.

Any.Do is The Best Way to Prioritize My Work. I have been using any.do now for over six years. I have tried many other applications to help me organize my to do list and set priorities. Any.do allows me to quickly move items from category to category and up and down within categories so that I can organize my daily tasks around high priorities. This allows me to stay focused on my most important priorities and related tasks so that I do not get distracted into activities that are less effective.
We all have a temptation to check items off our list for the satisfaction that brings. Checking the right tasks off the list, even if fewer tasks get done, is much more important than the volume of tasks. Any doubt do allows me to sortAnd shuffle multiple times a day to keep me focused.
I fact that any.do syncs with my email account, my slack account, and my calendar, and can be used on my phone and laptop, makes it a tool I can take and use anywhere. I highly recommend any doubt do to anyone who wants to get things done.
